I read `.standards/PROTOCOL.md`, `.standards/MODE.md`, `.standards/STATE.md`, and the Auditor's `.standards/CONTEXT.md`. The cycle is `export-20260924T090000Z-a7f3c1d2` in `SCOPING`, with the request: let administrators export the filtered records list as CSV; non-admins must not be able to export.

Before I can finish the scope I need one decision, which I've recorded in `Active Work.BlockedOn`:

When an administrator exports, should the service keep the CSV as a file (so the admin tool can hand it out), or only send the CSV back in the response? It changes what "done" means for access control: if files are kept, a refused request also has to leave no file behind.
Keep the files in the service, the admin tool hands them out. And yes, a refused request must not leave a file. Access has to be checked on the server, not in the UI.

Thanks. I recorded your answer and cleared the blocker.

The scope is complete at `.standards/docs/scope/export-20260924T090000Z-a7f3c1d2.md`:

- Goal: administrators can take the list they filtered by status, owner, or title text into a spreadsheet, and only administrators can create export files.
- Constraints: exports use the same filters and validation as `GET /records`; access is decided by the service; listing keeps its current behavior.
- Non-goals: other formats, column choice, scheduled or emailed exports, listing or removing old export files, front-end changes.
- Acceptance conditions:
  - `AC-001`: Administrators can export the currently filtered records as CSV; a field containing a comma, double quote, or newline is quoted per RFC 4180, with embedded double quotes doubled.
  - `AC-002`: An export request from a user who is not an administrator, or from no signed-in user, is denied by server-side authorization before any export file is created.
- Assumption: export files are kept by the service; how the admin tool offers them for download is outside this repository.
